_comment: Cluster topology for the rproxy. Point NODES_CONFIG at a copy of this.
Exactly one node must have "local": true -- that is the leader running
this process. It is never power-cycled, because it is what would have to
issue the power-off, so it needs no relay_uid or channel.
An Industrial Dual Relay Bricklet has two channels, so four workers need
two bricklets. relay_uid names which bricklet switches a node, and
channel (0 or 1) is the channel ON THAT BRICKLET -- not a cluster-wide
index. Numbering four workers 0,1,2,3 on one relay is rejected at
startup. Find the UIDs with Brick Viewer.
relay_uid may be omitted on a single-relay cluster, in which case
address         = the worker's tinyFaaS HTTP endpoint (function calls)
manager_address = the worker's management API (health checks, deploys)
